title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 697-698 of the 'suite à La Longue Marche'). Grothendieck studies the maximal abelian profinite cover U_∞ of U_{0,3} = P^1 - {0,1,∞}, i.e. the limit of the Fermat-curve tower F_n. Its group is F_∞° ≅ (Ẑ^{{0,1,∞}}/Ẑ) ⊗ Ẑ(1). This is the abelianization M^ of the geometric π_1, with Γ_Q acting through the cyclotomic character and S_3 acting by permuting {0,1,∞}.

On the previous page (230), the abelian cover is viewed as an F_∞°-torsor Û_∞(-J). On it, the arithmetic fundamental group M_{0,3} = π_1(U_{0,3,Q}, S_3; -J) of the quotient stack [U_{0,3}/S_3] (with base point J) acts compatibly with its action on F_∞°. That action factors through χ: M_{0,3} → Ẑ* and M_{0,3} → S_3.

This page:
(1) Finishes that sentence: the S_3-operations on the torsor are compatible with those on F_∞°.
(2) A crossed-out attempt says that torsors under groups M ⊗_Z T, with T an invertible Ẑ-module, are equivalently torsors under an affine group containing Ẑ*·M^. The intent is to recast the torsor-with-operations as a homomorphism into an affine group.
(3) Introduces (231), an exact sequence of group schemes over a base S_0: 1 → M → G_{ρ,σ}/μ_G → (G_m-type unit group) × (S_3)_{S_0} → 1, with the second map (χ, can). Here M is the rank-2 lattice and G_{ρ,σ} is a group built on generators ρ (order 3) and σ (order 2).
(4) Taking Ẑ-points and completing gives (232): 1 → M^ → G_{ρ,σ}/μ_G → Ẑ* × S_3 → 1. This recovers the action of Ẑ* × S_3 on M^ (cyclotomic twist plus permutation).
(5) Inside it is the extension (233): 1 → M^ → (·) → S_3 → 1. The next page identifies (233) as the quotient of (234), 1 → π_1(U_{0,3,Q̄}) → π_1(U_{0,3,Q̄}, S_3) → S_3 → 1, by the commutator subgroup of the free normal subgroup.

In modern terms, (234) is the profinite completion of 1 → Γ(2)/±1 → PSL_2(Z) = ⟨ρ, σ | ρ^3 = σ^2 = 1⟩ → S_3 → 1. This is the orbifold λ-line over the j-line. (233) is PSL_2(Z)^ modulo the derived subgroup of Γ(2)^ ('metabelian' level).

The goal (next page, (235)-(237)) is to identify G_{ρ,σ}/μ with the affine group Aff = (Ẑ* × S_3) ⋉ M^ inside Aff_Ẑ(M^). The structure (230) then becomes, up to non-unique isomorphism, a homomorphism M_{0,3} → Aff lifting (χ, pr). In other words, it is a 1-cocycle/Kummer class describing the Galois action on the abelianized orbifold π_1 with S_3-symmetric base point.
errors: The next page first asserts that (233) is non-split although its restrictions to ⟨ρ⟩ ≅ Z/3 and ⟨σ⟩ ≅ Z/2 split; it is then corrected in the margin ('si, elle est triviale, cf plus bas'). The correction is right. M ≅ Z^3/Z (with or without sign twist) is free as a Z[C_2]-module. As a Z[C_3]-module it is Z[ω], with Ĥ^0 = 0. So H^2 vanishes on both Sylow subgroups, hence H^2(S_3, M^) = 0 and (233) splits. The initial non-triviality claim was an error, which Grothendieck caught himself.
The precise nature of G_{ρ,σ}, μ_G and the unit group in (231) is not defined on this page. The derivation of (231) is left implicit, and the last lines of the page are only partially legible.

ideas.what: The maximal abelian (Fermat-tower) cover of P^1-{0,1,∞} as a torsor under (Ẑ^3/Ẑ)(1), with compatible action of the arithmetic π_1 of the S_3-quotient stack
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on H_1 of the Fermat tower / abelianized π_1 of the orbifold [P^1-{0,1,∞}/S_3]; Kummer cocycle
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (1980s, Fermat tower and Jacobi sums), Anderson, Coleman, Deligne (1989)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions S_3-action and the tower of Fermat curves in general terms; these details are unpublished

ideas.what: Extension 1 → M^ → PSL_2(Z)^/[Γ(2)^,Γ(2)^] → S_3 → 1 as a quotient of the orbifold fundamental-group extension
ideas.modern_name: Metabelian quotient of the profinite modular group PSL_2(Z)^ ≅ Z/2 * Z/3 completed
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Γ(2)/±1 free of rank 2, PSL_2(Z)/Γ(2) ≅ S_3)

ideas.what: Recasting a torsor under a twisted module M⊗T with compatible group actions as a homomorphism into the affine group (Ẑ*×S_3)⋉M^ lifting a given character
ideas.modern_name: Torsors with equivariant structure ↔ lifts to semidirect product / H^1 with twisted coefficients
ideas.where_published: general formalism in SGA 1 / Giraud's Cohomologie non abélienne (not this specific case)

missed.claim: The computation of the class of the M_{0,3}-equivariant torsor (the map M_{0,3} → Aff lifting (χ, pr)) for the S_3-symmetric base point J is set up but not carried out on this page. That class would encode Kummer classes attached to the orbifold points (6th/4th roots of unity). This is essentially known in the later literature on Galois actions on abelian/metabelian quotients, so the novelty is minimal.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is an explicit S_3-equivariant form of the abelian-level Galois action. It is of minor interest for GT/S_3-symmetric base points, but is largely covered by Ihara–Anderson–Deligne-type results.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but routine setup of the abelian (Fermat-tower) level of the Galois action on π_1 of the S_3-quotient of P^1-{0,1,∞}, i.e. the profinite modular group modulo Γ(2)''. The mathematics is classical or known, and the one false claim (non-splitness) is self-corrected.
transcription_corrections: The factor written 'O_12^*' in (231) is uncertain. Since it becomes Ẑ* after completion in (232), it is likely a multiplicative-group / unit group scheme (e.g. G_m or a units symbol), not literally O_12^*.
The annotation under (231) reads roughly '{H^+/μ_{S_0}' (with a struck character). It appears to describe (S_3)_{S_0} as a quotient H^+/μ, and is uncertain.
The middle term of (233) is a corrected, overwritten symbol, roughly '𝔊^{+∧}/μ_∞' (a completed group mod roots of unity), with an earlier crossed-out version beneath. It is not reliably '𝔖^{+∧}'.
The final lines read approximately 'qui est un quotient de la suite exacte dont trouvé[?] par[?]...'. They continue on the next page with (234), quotient 'par le sous-groupe des commutateurs'.
In the crossed-out passage, the affine group is written 'Ẑ^*.M^∧' (semidirect product of Ẑ* with M^), and the group 'M_{0,3}' appears after a struck '𝔖'.
